document.title: Harden zip bounds, header matching and JSON escaping
document.summary: Runtime Upload checks zip offsets without 32-bit wraparound, inflates entries in fixed chunks, matches HTTP headers case-insensitively at line starts, JSON-escapes response strings, and gains a CTest harness for all of it.
document.why: [Issue #43](source:s1) reports that 32-bit offset sums let an archive read out of bounds on the Vita, that lowercase `content-length`/`content-type` from Node `fetch` fail with 400/415, and that `package_name` reaches the JSON response unescaped.

sources.title: Harden Runtime Upload parsing: 32-bit zip offset overflow, case-sensitive headers, unescaped JSON
sources.gist: Overflow-checked zip offsets, case-insensitive headers, JSON escaping, plus a harness with traversal and overflow fixtures.

sources.label: PR #68
sources.gist: Stacked on #62; host tier passed in the Linux smoke Docker image.

lookFor: [The issue](source:s1) suggests `__builtin_add_overflow`; the change uses an `in_bounds(offset, len, size)` subtraction check instead, which needs no compiler builtin and gives the same guarantee.

groups.title: Zip offsets and per-entry allocation
groups.why: [#43](source:s1) shows `central_offset + central_size`, `local_offset + 30` and `data_offset + compressed_size` wrapping on ARM32, plus one `arena_alloc` of up to 64MB per entry.
groups.summary: Every attacker-controlled offset in `upload_archive_extract` now goes through `in_bounds`, and `write_deflated` streams into the output file instead of allocating the whole entry.
lookFor: Subtle: `local_offset + 30` was a `uint32_t` sum, so it wrapped on 64-bit hosts too; a central entry with `local_offset = 0xFFFFFFF0` segfaulted the old code and is now rejected with the invalid-local-data error.
The unpacked-limit check now runs before `total_unpacked` is incremented, so an entry declaring `0xFFFFFFFF` bytes cannot wrap a 32-bit running total back under 64MB.

A deflate stream that inflates past its declared `uncompressed_size` stops at the first 16KB chunk over the limit; the partial file stays in Runtime Upload Staging until the next `package_library_clear_staging`.

groups.title: Case-insensitive header lookup
groups.why: [#43](source:s1): Node `fetch` and undici send lowercase `content-length` and `content-type`, which the case-sensitive `strstr` lookup rejected.
groups.summary: `http_server.c` drops its `strstr`-based `header_value` and reads `Content-Length`, `Content-Type` and the multipart boundary through `upload_header_value` from the new `http_parse.c`.
lookFor: Behavior change no source names: `content_type_is` compares the media type before `;` exactly, so `multipart/form-data; boundary=application/zip` now takes the multipart path where the old `strstr` picked the raw-zip path.
`upload_content_length` returns -1 for `Content-Length: 12abc`, so such a request now gets 400 instead of being read as 12 bytes.
A `Content-Type` value longer than 255 bytes does not fit the copy buffer and is treated as absent, giving 415.

groups.title: JSON-escaped responses
groups.why: [#43](source:s1): `package_name` is injected into the JSON response unescaped.
groups.summary: `send_json_error` and the success body in `handle_upload` pass every string through `upload_json_escape` into buffers sized at 6x the input.

groups.title: upload_parsing_harness CTest
groups.why: [#43](source:s1) asks for a CTest harness covering request parsing and zip extraction, including traversal and overflow fixtures.
groups.summary: `tests/upload_parsing_harness.c` builds single-entry zips in memory with forged offsets and runs them through `upload_archive_extract`, and `CMakeLists.txt` registers it next to the other non-smoke harnesses.
lookFor: The harness links the real `package_library.c` and points it at a `mkdtemp` directory through `VITADECK_DATA_ROOT`, then removes that directory with `rm -rf` at exit.

commits.subject: test(upload): add upload parsing CTest harness
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Covers lowercase headers, a header name inside another header's value,
JSON escaping of quotes and backslashes, stored and deflated extraction,
a deflate stream larger than declared, wrapping central directory and
local header offsets, the unpacked limit, and a ../ traversal entry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(upload): JSON-escape strings placed into upload responses
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The package name and version were formatted into the success body
unescaped, so a name containing a quote or backslash produced invalid
JSON. Escape every string that goes into a JSON response, including
error codes and messages.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(upload): match HTTP headers case-insensitively at line starts
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Node fetch and undici send lowercase content-length and content-type,
which the case-sensitive lookup rejected with 400/415. Header lookup now
lives in http_parse.c, matches names case-insensitively only at line
starts, and copies the value bounded to its own line. Content-Type is
compared by media type rather than substring, so a boundary value can no
longer select the wrong body format.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(upload): bounds-check zip offsets without 32-bit wraparound
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Offsets read from the archive were added before comparing against the
archive size, which wraps on the Vita's 32-bit size_t. Compare with a
non-overflowing range check instead, guard the unpacked total the same
way, reject archives shorter than an EOCD record, and inflate entries in
fixed chunks straight to disk instead of allocating up to 64MB per entry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
